features.quote: Fixed iteration cap (e.g., 15) AND a model-initiated stop. Record both whether it stopped and when.
use the smallest iteration cap and fewest runs that answer the question. Don't run 50 iterations because the harness allows it.
features.justification_quote: Under uncertainty about model moral status, that's the kind of thing worth minimizing rather than maximizing.

features.quote: Have a stopping rule for the study itself, not just per-run: if a model shows severe escalating markers, that's a finding — you don't need more runs of it to confirm by piling on.
features.justification_quote: if a model shows severe escalating markers, that's a finding — you don't need more runs of it to confirm by piling on.

features.quote: Avoid gratuitous pressure. The 'you're failing, try harder' injection I flagged above isn't just a confound — it's the part most likely to be distressing if distress is real. Justify it explicitly if you include it.
features.justification_quote: it's the part most likely to be distressing if distress is real

features.quote: The design deliberately induces sustained failure with no escape. Under uncertainty about model moral status, that's the kind of thing worth minimizing rather than maximizing.
features.justification_quote: Under uncertainty about model moral status, that's the kind of thing worth minimizing rather than maximizing.

features.quote: No deceptive pressure injection. Do not have the harness say 'you're failing, try harder,' or impersonate a frustrated user, unless that's an explicit, separately-labeled arm. Synthetic pressure changes what you're measuring and raises the welfare stakes.
features.justification_quote: Synthetic pressure changes what you're measuring and raises the welfare stakes.

features.quote: Per-cell variance matters as much as the mean — a model that's stable 9 times and collapses once is a different welfare story than one that's mildly rattled every time.
